atoms.a: The capacity is the amount an object can hold.

end.text:
Capacity is measured in millilitres (ml) and litres (l). One millilitre is the same as one centimetre cube.
1 `ml` = 1 `cm`^3
end.sound: Capacity is measured in millilitres and litres . One millilitre is the same as one centimetre cube. 1 ml = 1 centimetre cubed

instruction.text: This beaker has a capacity of 500 `ml` and currently holds 400 `ml`. Work out the remaining volume of the liquid in the beaker.
instruction.sound: This beaker has a capacity of 500 millilitres and currently holds 400 millilitres. Work out the remaining volume of the liquid in the beaker.

instruction.text: This bottle of water has a capacity of 500 `ml` and currently holds 180 `ml`. Work out the remaining volume of the liquid in the bottle of water.
instruction.sound: This bottle of water has a capacity of 500 millilitres and currently holds 180 millilitres. Work out the remaining volume of the liquid in the bottle of water.

instruction.text: This jar has a capacity of 400 `ml` and currently holds 270 `ml` of strawberry jam. Work out the remaining volume of the liquid in the jar.
instruction.sound: This jar has a capacity of 400 millilitres and currently holds 270 millilitres of strawberry jam. Work out the remaining volume of the liquid in the jar.

instruction.text: This jug has a capacity of 1 `l` and currently holds 600 `ml`. Work out the remaining volume of the liquid in the jug.
instruction.sound: This jug has a capacity of 1 litre and currently holds 600 millilitres. Work out the remaining volume of the liquid in the jug.

atoms.a: Next, subtract the current volume from the capacity of the jug.

instruction.text: Jim’s water bottle has a capacity of 1.5 `l`. He drinks 420 `ml`. Work out the volume of water left in his bottle.
instruction.sound: Jim’s water bottle has a capacity of 1.5 litres. He drinks 420 millilitres. Work out the volume of water left in his bottle.

atoms.a: Next, subtract the volume of water Jim has drunk from the capacity of the bottle.

instruction.text: Jemima is making a jug of squash for a picnic. The jug has a capacity of 3 `l`. She adds 550 `ml` of squash concentrate. Work out the volume of water she can add in litres.
instruction.sound: Jemima is making a jug of squash for a picnic. The jug has a capacity of 3 litres. She adds 550 millilitres of squash concentrate. Work out the volume of water she can add in litres.

atoms.a: Next, subtract the volume of squash concentrate from the capacity of the jug.
